answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable stake: before an agent can trade, it must lock collateral and build a reputation history tied to real work, like a jetty that only admits ships that paid to dock. Sybil identities then face a real price — each fake must fund its own stake, and slashing burns it when the agent cheats. An ivory-tower identity check alone fails, but stake plus slashing makes mass fakery unprofitable: the attacker pays per identity, while honest agents pay once and keep earning.
